summary.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early forms join the sun and moon, associated with brightness or dawn, or the moon and a lattice window, interpreted as moonlight entering a room.

formation.text: The character has more than one reported early construction: 日 and 月 depict the sun and moon in a celestial image associated with brightness or dawn. The related form 朙 joins 月, the moon, with 囧, a lattice window, in an image interpreted as moonlight entering a room. 囧 is also proposed as a sound element in 朙, but that role is disputed.

components.text: In the early 日+月 form, 日 depicts the sun as part of a celestial image associated with brightness or, in one interpretation, dawn.
In the early 日+月 form, 月 depicts the moon as part of a celestial image associated with brightness or, in one interpretation, dawn.

In 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image. It is also proposed as a sound element, but the role is disputed: its reported Old Chinese reconstruction differs from 明’s, and the window’s ancient spoken name is not established.

sound_limitation.text: The proposed phonetic role remains unresolved. Neither the differing Old Chinese reconstructions nor the similar current Mandarin readings establish an ancient sound correspondence or recover the window’s spoken name.

sound.text: In current Mandarin, 囧 is jiǒng and 明 is míng. Their resemblance is a modern comparison and does not establish the ancient relationship.
In Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese, 囧 is reconstructed as *k-mraŋʔ and 明 as *mraŋ. The forms differ in initial and final, so this comparison alone does not demonstrate the proposed sound role.

components.text: In 朙, 月 depicts the moon in the interpretation of moonlight entering through a window.

history.text: Sun-and-moon forms are reported in oracle-bone and bronze writing. Other reported early forms include 朙, analyzed as 月 and 囧, and less secure 目+月 and 田+月 forms. Shuowen identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙, without making 朙 the sole early construction.
A Qin manuscript’s 目-form is reported as a likely graphic corruption of 囧. This proposed change concerns the written form; it does not resolve how the other early forms relate.

uncertainties.text: The reported early forms and readings have not been checked against inscription images, and exact dates for the cited examples remain unresolved.

senses.text: Brightness is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples. The evidence does not show whether this use preceded or followed the attested dawn use.
Dawn is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples; a Shijing line also illustrates daybreak. Its chronological relation to the brightness sense is unresolved.
Clear or manifest uses are reported in bronze inscriptions. How this sense developed from brightness or dawn is not shown.
Current meanings include bright, light, and clear.

limitations.text: The relative chronology of the early brightness and dawn uses, and the development of later clear or manifest uses, remain unresolved.

overview.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early forms pair the sun and moon, or the moon and a window; they are associated with brightness, dawn, or moonlight, but do not settle on one original meaning.

components.text: 日 pictures the sun in the early sun-and-moon form.
月 pictures the moon in the early sun-and-moon form.
In 朙, 囧 pictures a lattice window; its proposed sound role remains disputed.
In 朙, 月 pictures the moon in the moonlight-through-a-window interpretation.

relationships.text: In the reported early 日+月 form, 日 depicts the sun as part of the celestial image associated with 明.
In the reported early 日+月 form, 月 depicts the moon as part of the celestial image associated with 明.
Shuowen identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙, whose analysis joins 月 and 囧. This does not show that 朙 was the only early form.
In 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image.
In 朙, 月 depicts the moon in the reported moonlight-through-a-window interpretation.

囧 is proposed as a sound element in 朙. In Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese, 囧 *k-mraŋʔ and 明 *mraŋ differ in initial and final; current Mandarin jiǒng and míng resemble one another but do not settle the historical analysis.
